text:
Maya P: Ran a focused loadbench against staging last night to validate RPM/TPM defaults and burst handling. Wanted to share results and get input before we bake anything into prod.

Liam H: awesome — was this against the public API or a staging-only key?

Maya P: staging-only API key (stg-load-01). Test targeted /v1/generate with a 512 token average response. Workload was a mix: 60% single-turn prompts, 40% streaming chat.

Sanjay R: curious about tooling + commands you used.

Maya P: used vegeta for concurrency control and a simple token-generation shim to approximate tokens/response. Command:```bash
echo "POST /v1/generate" | vegeta attack -rate 100 -duration 10m | vegeta report
``` then we converted RPS->RPM and estimated TPM by multiplying by 512 tokens.

Kelly (SRE): did you hit 429s or auth errs? Any billing anomalies flagged?

Maya P: yes — at sustained 1,000 RPM we started seeing 429s around minute 3. Burst window allowed short spikes up to ~1.6k RPM for <30s. After sustained period, token bucket depleted and throttles enforced. No 401s. BillingBot emitted a quota alert at 1769004380 (quota_exhausted: true) — tagging logs.

Jade - Support: customers have complained about unexpected 429s when they do short bursts; is this the same behavior? Any way to replicate for support repro steps?

Maya P: repro steps I recorded: 1) create staging key with per-minute limit 1k RPM; 2) run a burst script:```bash
for i in {1..10}; do seq -f "POST /v1/generate" 200 | vegeta attack -rate 200 -duration 10s; sleep 5; done
``` 3) watch headers: `x-rw-ratelimit-remaining` goes negative, responses 429 include `Retry-After`. Paste logs:```
429 responses start at 00:03:12, 95% p95 latency jumps from 120ms -> 900ms before 429s.
```

Liam H: ok. Two questions: a) are limits enforced per-key or per-route? b) what's the current burst token bucket config (burst_size, refill_rate, window)?

Sanjay R: from config: default is per-key global (not per-route). Burst bucket: burst_size=2000 tokens, refill_rate=1000 tokens/min, window=60s (effectively allows ~2000 tokens immediate). But tokens here map to per-request tokens, not downstream model tokens — need mapping clarity.

Kelly (SRE): important point — our billing TPM counts model tokens. Rate limiter counts requests (or modeled tokens) depending on route. That mismatch explains some customer confusion. We should ensure defaults reflect both request RPM and token TPM.

Jade - Support: for support-run repros can we standardize a short script that produces the same 429 pattern so L2 can reproduce in a sandbox? Could be useful for escalations.

Maya P: yes I'll drop a compact repro gist and also add a small script that hits both the short request-rate limit and a token-based limit. Proposed sane defaults from bench: - default RPM: 600 (sustained) - soft burst RPM: 1800 for 20s - default TPM: 120k tokens/min (for 512 token responses that's ~235 RPM equivalent)

Liam H: that TPM feels low if customers stream long contexts. Maybe make TPM adaptive by model profile (short-chat vs long-completion). We could pick conservative global defaults and recommend per-customer overrides.

Sanjay R: agree. Proposal: keep global safe defaults (RPM=600, TPM=120k), expose per-customer bump and automatic per-route limits (e.g., embeddings vs chat) in the console. Also add observability: token burn rate and bucket fill metrics per key.

Kelly (SRE): action items: 1) Maya: drop repro script + vegeta/locust commands + a short readme for support (ETA EOD). 2) Ops: add metric `rate_limiter.bucket_level` with tags {key, route}. 3) Product: doc changes to explain RPM vs TPM and burst semantics.

Maya P: noted — I'll post the gist and a staging key for qa. Quick snippet I'll share now for support:```bash
# short burst test, expects 429s after bucket drains
for i in {1..6}; do curl -s -X POST $STG_URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $STG_KEY" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' & done; sleep 3; done
```

Kelly (SRE): I'll file the infra ticket to record current bucket params + add the metric. Ticket: INF-2381.

Jade - Support: thanks — that repro will help triage. Also please include the exact `x-rw-ratelimit-*` header examples so we can train the support KB.

ops-bot: Deploy window scheduled for 2026-04-05 02:00 UTC to roll default rate-limiter changes to staging only.

Maya P: final thought — we should probably add a grace period on new keys: initial ramp for 10 minutes where burst allowance is increased 2x to prevent early churn for new signups. Thoughts?

Liam H: like it, but make it opt-in per-customer until we have more confidence. Could be a product flag.

Sanjay R: +1. I'll prototype feature flag and simulate with the same loadbench.

Jade - Support: leaving a note to update KB after flag is tested.

BillingBot: Quota alert cleared at 1769004445 for stg-load-01 (quota restored).

Maya P: thanks everyone — I'll upload artifacts and post the gist link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
